_comment: Runnable example with INVENTED figures - the IN-SERVICE path (a rental that was placed in service, not sold). No sale/schedule_d block; a `depreciation` block instead. Never put a real client's numbers in this repo.

purchase._placed_in_service_note: Set this once the property is genuinely in service. Its YEAR must match the purchase year for the template to expense the operating costs; a different year (or blank) capitalizes them into basis instead.
notes: PREFILLED FROM: ALTA Settlement Statement, File EXAMPLE-003.
Buyer EXAMPLE RENTALS LLC. Financed - see the Loan Costs block.
PLACED IN SERVICE 10/01/2025 - first tenant. Depreciation starts
then, on the Depreciation tab. Loan costs amortize over the loan
term separately; they are NOT part of the depreciable building.

depreciation._comment: class is 'residential' (27.5 yr) or 'nonresidential' (39 yr). A rental whose AVERAGE stay is 30 days or more is residential; 7 days or less makes it nonresidential 39-year. Ask before assuming.
depreciation.intro: Placed in service October 2025. Land is split off the county appraisal RATIO (not its dollar amount) and never depreciates; the building runs 27.5-year straight line on the mid-month convention.
notes: THE APPRAISAL SETS THE RATIO, NOT THE DOLLARS
The county's assessed values are usually below what was paid. Only
their land-to-building PROPORTION is used; it is applied to the
actual cost basis, so the split always adds back to what was paid.
Real property is treated as placed in service mid-month whatever the
actual day, so an October date gives 2.5 months in year one.
The year-1 rate shown ties to IRS Table A-6 (27.5 yr) / A-7a (39 yr).
WHAT IS *NOT* IN THE BUILDING BASIS
Loan costs amortize over the loan term as a separate intangible.
Escrow deposits are an asset, released as the lender pays the bills.

mapping.treatment: Basis of the property, split land/building by the appraisal ratio.
Amortized over the loan term - NOT building basis, so it never reaches the depreciation schedule.
Current asset. Not a cost until the lender pays the bill.
